quotes.text: "My dear Scrooge, how are you? When will you come to see me?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "No eye at all is better than an evil eye, dark master!"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "A merry Christmas, uncle! God save you!"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "You don't mean that, I am sure?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "'Merry Christmas'! What right have you to be merry? What reason have you to be merry? You're poor enough."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "What right have you to be dismal? What reason have you to be morose? You're rich enough."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "when I live in such a world of fools as this? Merry Christmas! Out upon merry Christmas! What's Christmas time to you but a time for paying bills without money; a time for finding yourself a year older, but not an hour richer; a time for balancing your books and having every item in 'em through a round dozen of months presented dead against you? If I could work my will"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "every idiot who goes about with 'Merry Christmas' on his lips should be boiled with his own pudding, and buried with a stake of holly through his heart. He should!"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Keep Christmas in your own way, and let me keep it in mine."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Much good may it do you! Much good it has ever done you!"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "There are many things from which I might have derived good, by which I have not profited, I dare say"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Christmas among the rest. But I am sure I have always thought of Christmas time, when it has come round—apart from the veneration due to its sacred name and origin, if anything belonging to it can be apart from that—as a good time; a kind, forgiving, charitable, pleasant time; the only time I know of, in the long calendar of the year, when men and women seem by one consent to open their shut–up hearts freely, and to think of people below them as if they really were fellow–passengers to the grave, and not another race of creatures bound on other journeys. And therefore, uncle, though it has never put a scrap of gold or silver in my pocket, I believe that it has done me good, and will do me good; and I say, God bless it!"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Let me hear another sound from you"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "and you'll keep your Christmas by losing your situation! You're quite a powerful speaker, sir"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "I wonder you don't go into Parliament."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Don't be angry, uncle. Come! Dine with us tomorrow."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Nay, uncle, but you never came to see me before that happened. Why give it as a reason for not coming now?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "I want nothing from you; I ask nothing of you; why cannot we be friends?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "I am sorry, with all my heart, to find you so resolute. We have never had any quarrel, to which I have been a party. But I have made the trial in homage to Christmas, and I'll keep my Christmas humour to the last. So a merry Christmas, uncle!"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "My clerk, with fifteen shillings a week, and a wife and family, talking about a merry Christmas. I'll retire to Bedlam."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Have I the pleasure of addressing Mr. Scrooge or Mr. Marley?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Mr. Marley has been dead these seven years"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "He died seven years ago, this very night."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "We have no doubt his liberality is well represented by his surviving partner"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "At this festive season of the year, Mr. Scrooge"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "it is more than usually desirable that we should make some slight provision for the poor and destitute, who suffer greatly at the present time. Many thousands are in want of common necessaries; hundreds of thousands are in want of common comforts, sir."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "I wish I could say they were not."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "The Treadmill and the Poor Law are in full vigour, then?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Oh! I was afraid, from what you said at first, that something had occurred to stop them in their useful course"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Under the impression that they scarcely furnish Christian cheer of mind or body to the multitude"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "a few of us are endeavouring to raise a fund to buy the poor some meat and drink, and means of warmth. We choose this time, because it is a time, of all others, when want is keenly felt, and abundance rejoices. What shall I put you down for?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Since you ask me what I wish, gentlemen, that is my answer. I don't make merry myself at Christmas and I can't afford to make idle people merry. I help to support the establishments I have mentioned—they cost enough; and those who are badly off must go there."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Many can't go there; and many would rather die."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "they had better do it, and decrease the surplus population. Besides—excuse me—I don't know that."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "It's enough for a man to understand his own business, and not to interfere with other people's. Mine occupies me constantly. Good afternoon, gentlemen!"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "God bless you, merry gentlemen! May nothing you dismay!"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "You'll want all day tomorrow, I suppose?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "and it's not fair. If I was to stop you half–a–crown for it, you'd think yourself ill–used, I'll be bound?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "you don't think me ill–used, when I pay a day's wages for no work."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "A poor excuse for picking a man's pocket every twenty–fifth of December!"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "But I suppose you must have the whole day. Be here all the earlier next morning."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "In life I was your partner, Jacob Marley."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "What evidence would you have of my reality beyond that of your senses?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "a little thing affects them. A slight disorder of the stomach makes them cheats. You may be an undigested bit of beef, a blot of mustard, a crumb of cheese, a fragment of an underdone potato. There's more of gravy than of grave about you, whatever you are!"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "I have but to swallow this, and be for the rest of my days persecuted by a legion of goblins, all of my own creation. Humbug, I tell you! humbug!"

quotes.text: "Dreadful apparition, why do you trouble me?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "I wear the chain I forged in life"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "I made it link by link, and yard by yard; I girded it on of my own free will, and of my own free will I wore it. Is its pattern strange to you?"

quotes.text: "the weight and length of the strong coil you bear yourself? It was full as heavy and as long as this, seven Christmas Eves ago. You have laboured on it, since. It is a ponderous chain!"

quotes.text: "Old Jacob Marley, tell me more. Speak comfort to me, Jacob!"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "It comes from other regions, Ebenezer Scrooge, and is conveyed by other ministers, to other kinds of men. Nor can I tell you what I would. A very little more is all permitted to me. I cannot rest, I cannot stay, I cannot linger anywhere. My spirit never walked beyond our counting–house—mark me!—in life my spirit never roved beyond the narrow limits of our money–changing hole; and weary journeys lie before me!"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "You must have been very slow about it, Jacob"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "No rest, no peace. Incessant torture of remorse."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "You might have got over a great quantity of ground in seven years"

quotes.text: "not to know, that ages of incessant labour by immortal creatures, for this earth must pass into eternity before the good of which it is susceptible is all developed. Not to know that any Christian spirit working kindly in its little sphere, whatever it may be, will find its mortal life too short for its vast means of usefulness. Not to know that no space of regret can make amends for one life's opportunity misused! Yet such was I! Oh! such was I!"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "But you were always a good man of business, Jacob"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Mankind was my business. The common welfare was my business; charity, mercy, forbearance, and benevolence, were, all, my business. The dealings of my trade were but a drop of water in the comprehensive ocean of my business!"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "At this time of the rolling year"

quotes.text: "I suffer most. Why did I walk through crowds of fellow–beings with my eyes turned down, and never raise them to that blessed Star which led the Wise Men to a poor abode! Were there no poor homes to which its light would have conducted me!"

quotes.text: "But don't be hard upon me! Don't be flowery, Jacob! Pray!"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "How it is that I appear before you in a shape that you can see, I may not tell. I have sat invisible beside you many and many a day."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "That is no light part of my penance"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "I am here tonight to warn you, that you have yet a chance and hope of escaping my fate. A chance and hope of my procuring, Ebenezer."

quotes.text: "You were always a good friend to me"

quotes.text: "Is that the chance and hope you mentioned, Jacob?"

quotes.text: "This is the even-handed dealing of the world!"

quotes.text: "Even if I have grown so much wiser, what then? I am not changed towards you."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Our contract is an old one. It was made when we were both poor and content to be so, until, in good season, we could improve our worldly fortune by our patient industry. You are changed. When it was made, you were another man."

quotes.text: "Your own feeling tells you that you were not what you are,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "I am. That which promised happiness when we were one in heart, is fraught with misery now that we are two. How often and how keenly I have thought of this, I will not say. It is enough that I have thought of it, and can release you."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "In a changed nature; in an altered spirit; in another atmosphere of life; another Hope as its great end. In everything that made my love of any worth or value in your sight. If this had never been between us,"

quotes.text: "O would gladly think otherwise if I could,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Heaven knows! When I have learned a Truth like this, I know how strong and irresistible it must be. I do; and I release you. With a full heart, for the love of him you once were."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "You may—the memory of what is past half makes me hope you will—have pain in this. A very, very brief time, and you will dismiss the recollection of it, gladly, as an unprofitable dream, from which it happened well that you awoke. May you be happy in the life you have chosen!"

quotes.text: "He has given us plenty of merriment, I am sure,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "and it would be ungrateful not to drink his health. Here is a glass of mulled wine ready to our hand at the moment; and I say, 'Uncle Scrooge!'"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "A Merry Christmas and a Happy New Year to the old man, whatever he is!"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "He wouldn't take it from me, but may he have it, nevertheless. Uncle Scrooge!"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "My life upon this globe, is very brief,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "To-night at midnight. Hark! The time is drawing near."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Forgive me if I am not justified in what I ask,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "but I see something strange, and not belonging to yourself, protruding from your skirts. Is it a foot or a claw?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "It might be a claw, for the flesh there is upon it,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Oh, Man! look here. Look, look, down here!"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "And they cling to me, appealing from their fathers. This boy is Ignorance. This girl is Want. Beware them both, and all of their degree, but most of all beware this boy, for on his brow I see that written which is Doom, unless the writing be erased. Deny it!"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Slander those who tell it ye! Admit it for your factious purposes, and make it worse. And bide the end!"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "I am in the presence of the Ghost of Christmas Yet To Come?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "You are about to show me shadows of the things that have not happened, but will happen in the time before us,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "I fear you more than any Spectre I have seen. But, as I know your purpose is to do me good, and as I hope to live to be another man from what I was, I am prepared to bear you company, and do it with a thankful heart. Will you not speak to me?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Lead on! The night is waning fast, and it is precious time to me, I know. Lead on, Spirit!"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "I don't know much about it, either way. I only know he's dead."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Why, what was the matter with him?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "What has he done with his money?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Left it to his Company, perhaps. He hasn't left it to me. That's all know."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "It's likely to be a very cheap funeral,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "for upon my life I don't know of anybody to go to it. Suppose we make up a party and volunteer?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "I don't mind going if a lunch is provided,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "But I must be fed, if I make one."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Well, I am the most disinterested among you, after all,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "for I never wear black gloves, and I never eat lunch. But I'll offer to go, if anybody else will. When I come to think of it, I'm not at all sure that I wasn't his most particular friend; for we used to stop and speak whenever we met. Bye, bye!"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Old Scratch has got his own at last, hey?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Seasonable for Christmas time. You're not a skaiter, I suppose?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "No. No. Something else to think of. Good morning!"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Let the charwoman alone to be the first!"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Let the laundress alone to be the second; and let the undertaker's man alone to be the third. Look here, old Joe, here's a chance! If we haven't all three met here without meaning it!"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "You couldn't have met in a better place,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Come into the parlour. You were made free of it long ago, you know; and the other two an't strangers. Stop till I shut the door of the shop. Ah! How it skreeks! There an't such a rusty bit of metal in the place as its own hinges, I believe; and I'm sure there's no such old bones here, as mine. Ha, ha! We're all suitable to our calling, we're well matched. Come into the parlour. Come into the parlour."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "What odds then! What odds, Mrs. Dilber?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Every person has a right to take care of themselves. He always did!"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Why, then, don't stand staring as if you was afraid, woman; who's the wiser? We're not going to pick holes in each other's coats, I suppose?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "That's enough. Who's the worse for the loss of a few things like these? Not a dead man, I suppose."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "If he wanted to keep 'em after he was dead, a wicked old screw,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "why wasn't he natural in his lifetime? If he had been, he'd have had somebody to look after him when he was struck with Death, instead of lying gasping out his last there, alone by himself."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "It's the truest word that ever was spoke,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "I wish it was a little heavier one,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "and it should have been, you may depend upon it, if I could have laid my hands on anything else. Open that bundle, old Joe, and let me know the value of it. Speak out plain. I'm not afraid to be the first, nor afraid for them to see it. We knew pretty well that we were helping ourselves, before we met here, I believe. It's no sin. Open the bundle, Joe."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "and I wouldn't give another sixpence, if I was to be boiled for not doing it. Who's next?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "I always give too much to ladies. It's a weakness of mine, and that's the way I ruin myself,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "That's your account. If you asked me for another penny, and made it an open question, I'd repent of being so liberal, and knock off half-a-crown."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "You don't mean to say you took 'em down, rings and all, with him lying there?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "You were born to make your fortune,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "I certainly shan't hold my hand, when I can get anything in it by reaching it out, for the sake of such a man as He was, I promise you, Joe,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Don't drop that oil upon the blankets, now."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "He isn't likely to take cold without 'em, I dare say."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "I hope he didn't die of anything catching? Eh?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "I an't so fond of his company that I'd loiter about him for such things, if he did. Ah! You may look through that shirt till your eyes ache; but you won't find a hole in it, nor a threadbare place. It's the best he had, and a fine one too. They'd have wasted it, if it hadn't been for me."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "What do you call wasting of it?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Putting it on him to be buried in, to be sure,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Somebody was fool enough to do it, but I took it off again. If calico an't good enough for such a purpose, it isn't good enough for anything. It's quite as becoming to the body. He can't look uglier than he did in that one."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "This is the end of it, you see! He frightened every one away from him when he was alive, to profit us when he was dead! Ha, ha, ha!"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "I see, I see. The case of this unhappy man might be my own. My life tends that way, now. Merciful Heaven, what is this!"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "this is a fearful place. In leaving it, I shall not leave its lesson, trust me. Let us go!"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "and I would do it, if I could. But I have not the power, Spirit. I have not the power."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "If there is any person in the town, who feels emotion caused by this man's death,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "show that person to me, Spirit, I beseech you!"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "there is! Nothing is past hope, if such a miracle has happened."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "What the half-drunken woman whom I told you of last night, said to me, when I tried to see him and obtain a week's delay; and what I thought was a mere excuse to avoid me; turns out to have been quite true. He was not only very ill, but dying, then."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "To whom will our debt be transferred?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "I don't know. But before that time we shall be ready with the money; and even though we were not, it would be bad fortune indeed to find so merciless a creditor in his successor. We may sleep to-night with light hearts, Caroline!"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Let me see some tenderness connected with a death,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "or that dark chamber, Spirit, which we left just now, will be for ever present to me."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "'And He took a child, and set him in the midst of them.'"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "It makes them weak by candle-light; and I wouldn't show weak eyes to your father when he comes home, for the world. It must be near his time."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "But I think he's walked a little slower than he used, these few last evenings, mother."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "I have known him walk with—I have known him walk with Tiny Tim upon his shoulder, very fast indeed."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "But he was very light to carry,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "and his father loved him so, that it was no trouble—no trouble. And there is your father at the door!"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Don't mind it, father. Don't be grieved!"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "I wish you could have gone. It would have done you good to see how green a place it is. But you'll see it often. I promised him that I would walk there on a Sunday. My little, little child!"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "for he is the pleasantest-spoken gentleman you ever heard, I told him. 'I am heartily sorry for it, Mr. Cratchit, he said, 'and heartily sorry for your good wife.' By the bye, how he ever knew that, I don't know."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Why, that you were a good wife,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "I hope they do. 'Heartily sorry,' he said. 'for your good wife. If I can be of service in you in any way,' he said, giving me his card, 'that's where I live. Pray come to me.' Now, it wasn't,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "for the sake of anything he might be able to do for us, so much as for his kind way, that this was quite delightful. It really seemed as if he had known our Tiny Tim, and felt with us."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "You would be surer of it, my dear,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "if you saw and spoke to him. I shouldn't be at all surprised, mark what I say, if he got Peter a better situation."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Peter will be keeping company with some one, and setting up for himself."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "one of these days; though there's plenty of time for that, my dear. But however and whenever we part from one another, I am sure we shall none of us forget poor Tiny Tim—shall we—or this first parting that there was among us?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "I know, my dears, that when we recollect how patient and how mild he was; although he was a little, little child; we shall not quarrel easily among ourselves, and forget poor Tiny Tim in doing it."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "something informs me that our parting moment is at hand. I know it, but I know not how. Tell me what man that was whom we saw lying dead?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "through which we hurry now, is where my place of occupation is, and has been for a length of time. I see the house. Let me behold what I shall be, in days to come."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Before I draw nearer to that stone to which you point,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "answer me one question. Are these the shadows of the things that Will be, or are they shadows of the things that May be, only?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Men's courses will foreshadow certain ends, to which, if persevered in, they must lead,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "But if the courses be departed from, the ends will change. Say it is thus with what you show me!"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Am I that man who lay upon the bed?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "hear me! I am not the man I was. I will not be the man I must have been but for this intercourse. Why show me this, if I am past all hope?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Your nature intercedes for me, and pities me. Assure me that I yet may change these shadows you have shown me, by an altered life!"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "I will honour Christmas in my heart, and try to keep it all the year. I will live in the Past, the Present, and the Future. The Spirits of all Three shall strive within me. I will not shut out the lessons that they teach. Oh, tell me I may sponge away the writing on this stone!"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "I will live in the Past, the Present, and the Future!"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "The Spirits of all Three shall strive within me. Oh Jacob Marley! Heaven, and the Christmas Time be praised for this! I say it on my knees, old Jacob; on my knees!"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "they are not torn down, rings and all. They are here: I am here: the shadows of the things that would have been, may be dispelled. They will be. I know they will!"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "I am as light as a feather, I am as happy as an angel, I am as merry as a school-boy. I am as giddy as a drunken man. A merry Christmas to everybody! A happy New Year to all the world. Hallo here! Whoop! Hallo!"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "There's the saucepan that the gruel was in!"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "There's the door, by which the Ghost of Jacob Marley entered! There's the corner where the Ghost of Christmas Present sat! There's the window where I saw the wandering Spirits! It's all right, it's all true, it all happened. Ha ha ha!"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "I don't know what day of the month it is!"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "I don't know how long I've been among the Spirits. I don't know anything. I'm quite a baby. Never mind. I don't care. I'd rather be a baby. Hallo! Whoop! Hallo here!"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "I haven't missed it. The Spirits have done it all in one night. They can do anything they like. Of course they can. Of course they can. Hallo, my fine fellow!"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Do you know the Poulterer's, in the next street but one, at the corner?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "A remarkable boy! Do you know whether they've sold the prize Turkey that was hanging up there? Not the little prize Turkey: the big one?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "What, the one as big as me?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "It's a pleasure to talk to him. Yes, my buck!"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "I am in earnest. Go and buy it, and tell 'em to bring it here, that I may give them the direction where to take it. Come back with the man, and I'll give you a shilling. Come back with him in less than five minutes, and I'll give you half-a-crown!"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "He sha'n't know who sends it. It's twice the size of Tiny Tim. Joe Miller never made such a joke as sending it to Bob's will be!"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "I shall love it, as long as I live!"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "I scarcely ever looked at it before. What an honest expression it has in its face! It's a wonderful knocker!—Here's the Turkey. Hallo! Whoop! How are you! Merry Christmas!"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Why, it's impossible to carry that to Camden Town,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Good morning, sir! A merry Christmas to you!"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "How do you do? I hope you succeeded yesterday. It was very kind of you. A merry Christmas to you, sir!"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "That is my name, and I fear it may not be pleasant to you. Allow me to ask your pardon. And will you have the goodness"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "My dear Mr. Scrooge, are you serious?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Not a farthing less. A great many back-payments are included in it, I assure you. Will you do me that favour?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "I don't know what to say to such munifi—"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Come and see me. Will you come and see me?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "I am much obliged to you. I thank you fifty times. Bless you!"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Is your master at home, my dear?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "He's in the dining-room, sir, along with mistress. I'll show you up stairs, if you please."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "It's I. Your uncle Scrooge. I have come to dinner. Will you let me in, Fred?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "What do you mean by coming here at this time of day?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Yes. I think you are. Step this way, if you please."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "It shall not be repeated. I was making rather merry yesterday, sir."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Now, I'll tell you what, my friend,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "I am not going to stand this sort of thing any longer. And therefore,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "and therefore I am about to raise your salary!"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "A merrier Christmas, Bob, my good fellow, than I have given you, for many a year! I'll raise your salary, and endeavour to assist your struggling family, and we will discuss your affairs this very afternoon, over a Christmas bowl of smoking bishop, Bob!  Make up the fires, and buy another coal-scuttle before you dot another i, Bob Cratchit!"
quotes.speaker: Unknown
